record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: Let G be a finite directed or undirected graph, and let lambda(G) be the number of vertices in a longest path of G. For every natural number q with 0 < q < lambda(G), must the vertices of G be partitionable into two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs A and B such that lambda(A) is at most q and lambda(B) is at most lambda(G) - q?

evidence.quote: A partition of G is a pair (A, B) of vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs of G such that V (A)∪ V (B) = V (G). Let λ(D) denote the number of vertices in a longest path of D.
Conjecture 4.1 Let G be a directed or undirected graph. For every natural number q with 0 < q < λ(G) there is a partition (A, B) of G such that λ(A) ≤ q and λ(B) ≤ λ(G) − q.
For undirected graph, the conjecture was first formulated in 1981 (see [37]), and it is still open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite graph, either undirected or directed. A partition of $G$ is an ordered pair $(A,B)$ of vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs of $G$ with $V(A)\cup V(B)=V(G)$. For a graph (or digraph) $H$, let $\lambda(H)$ denote the number of vertices in a longest path of $H$ (in the directed case, a longest directed path). 

Prove or disprove: For every finite (directed or undirected) graph $G$ and every natural number $q$ with $0<q<\lambda(G)$, there exists a partition $(A,B)$ of $G$ such that
$$\lambda(A)\le q \quad\text{and}\quad \lambda(B)\le \lambda(G)-q.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The undirected Path Partition Conjecture, first formulated in 1981, remains open. The directed analogue (Directed Path Partition Conjecture) is also still open in general, with only partial results established for special classes of digraphs (e.g., claw-free graphs, locally in-semicomplete digraphs, quasi-transitive digraphs).

status_evidence.title: The Path Partition Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the Path Partition Conjecture, which remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The Path Partition Conjecture is still open.

status_evidence.title: Some digraph classes that meet the directed path partition conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Several classes of digraphs are shown to satisfy DPPC, motivated by the conjecture being unresolved in general.
status_evidence.claim: DPPC is proven only for special digraph classes; general case open.

status_evidence.title: The Path Partition Conjecture is true for claw-free graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes PPC for claw-free graphs, indicating general case unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist; conjecture not settled in general.
